subject: Per-request unit cost matrix & MAP checkpoints
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Per-request unit cost matrix & MAP checkpoints

Emily — attaching a first-pass per-request unit-cost matrix (xlsx) and a compact MAP checklist (pdf). Goal: make the MAP explicit about the unit economics checks we need to validate before close so procurement + engineering have a shared acceptance criteria. High-level asks: 

- Confirm the representative traffic profile (attached acme-usage-sample.json) — particularly percentage of short context queries (<=128 tokens) vs long (>=1024).
- Confirm acceptable latency SLOs for baseline and peak (P50/P95).
- Agree on the caching hypothesis we should run in the pilot (session KV prefix cache vs request-level dedupe).
- Approve the evaluation prompt set (we'll provide a small canonical set) and the target pass rates for quality regressions.

Key notes in the matrix: tokens-per-request estimates, estimated cache hit rates (placeholder), batching window assumptions (we recommend 20–50ms in general), and fallback model variants for graceful degradation. These are conservative defaults; we'll run smoke tests to get real numbers.

Can you review and get back with any edits by Monday 24 May? If we align, we can fold this into the MAP and lock the close timeline.

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: per-request-cost-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP-checklist-v2.pdf (PDF)

From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>

Cc: Sally Turner <sally.turner@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-request unit cost matrix & MAP checkpoints

Thanks, Karthik — quick read-through looks helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we finalize the MAP: 

1) Caching: when you say "KV prefix cache" are you proposing session continuity caching (user session across requests) or request-level common-prefix cache? Our use case is mostly single-turn API calls but many share the same patient metadata prefix. How should we model hit rates?

2) Batching: do your batching window guidance (20–50ms) assume thin-client routing from our side (i.e., requests can be buffered) or is that strictly server-side batching? If client buffering is required, we need to check product constraints.

3) Quantization/model variants: we need to understand uplift/loss tradeoffs — what's the expected delta in quality at 4-bit quant vs int8 dynamic quant? Any existing evals you can point to?

I attached a short sample of our real traffic (acme-usage-sample.json) — it's a 48‑hour slice with per-request token distributions. I can share more if needed. Goal for us is to avoid overprovisioning in Commit PO and have concrete gating for go/no-go.

Emily
Director, Data Platforms
Acme HealthTech

Attachment: acme-usage-sample.json (48h sample)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-request unit cost matrix & MAP checkpoints

Emily — thanks for the sample, that's exactly what we need. A few concrete answers and a proposed MAP gating plan below. TL;DR: we can be conservative in the PO and run a 2-week pilot to validate the matrix with minimal risk.

Caching (how to model hit rates):
- Two levels: prefix-level (common patient metadata) and session-level (multi-turn). For your workload (single-turn with shared prefixes), model a realistic prefix-hit of 30–45% initially; we'll run traffic replay to get an empirical number. If prefixes are highly templated, hit rates can approach 60% but don't assume that until verified.

Batching assumptions (server-side continuous batching):
- The 20–50ms window is server-side and conservative; it assumes a continuous batching runtime and ~8–12 concurrent inflight requests per GPU shard. If you can do client-side micro-batching (buffering 5–10ms), savings improve but adds integration complexity.

Quantization impact (high-level):
- 8-bit dynamic quant typically has <2% quality delta vs FP16 on classification/LM tasks we tested. 4-bit quant (Q4) can introduce more variation — plan for a small eval set to measure. For MAP gating, we suggest: baseline on FP16, cost variant on Q4x to measure delta.

Proposed MAP gating (milestones):
- Milestone A (Pilot start): deploy smoke cluster with your 48h replay (week 0), collect raw tokens/latency/caching stats. Acceptance = observed token rate within +/-20% of matrix and cache hit >= modeled min (30%).
- Milestone B (MAP eval): run evaluation prompts (we'll provide 200 canonical prompts) and measure quality delta (target: <=5% regression on key metrics).
- Milestone C (Close readiness): confirm invoices/PO terms with procurement and agreed rollback plan.

Immediate asks from Acme:
- Confirm target P95 latency (we recommend <450ms for the primary flows).
- Confirm test account for replay and a contact for procurement to loop in.

We can run a quick smoke test next week. Karthik / Laura — can you take point on the replay script and the evaluation prompt set? I'll coordinate with the infra team to reserve a small dedicated pool for the pilot.

—Rishi
VP, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
